header.running_head: 3. The Rights and Duties of Muslims

blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said: “Give gifts to one another! A gift removes the rancour of the heart. No woman should look down upon the gift of her neighbouring woman, even if it is a piece of a sheep's trotter!” (In the same way, the woman giving the gift should not regard this gift as trivial either.)

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ ذَرٍّ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: لَا يَحْقِرَنَّ اَحَدُكُمْ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْمَعْرُوْفِ، وَاِنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَلْيَلْقَ اَخَاهُ بِوَجْهٍ طَلِيْقٍ، وَاِنِ اشْتَرَيْتَ لَحْمًا اَوْ طَبَخْتَ قِدْرًا فَاكْثِرْ مَرَقَتَهُ وَاغْرِفْ لِجَارِكَ مِنْهُ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه الترمذي وقال: هذا حديث حسن صحيح باب ماجاء في اكثار ماء المرقة رقم: ١٨٣٣
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said: “None of you should regard even a small good deed as trivial. If one is unable to do any good, then meeting one's brother with a cheerful face is also a good deed. If you buy meat to cook, or cook some curry, increase its quantity, and give a little of it to your neighbour as well.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ اَنَّ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ ﷺ قَالَ: لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مَنْ لَا يَاْمَنُ جَارُهُ بَوَائِقَهُ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه مسلم باب بيان تحريم ايذاء الجار رقم:١٧٢
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) has narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The one whose neighbour is not safe from his harm will not enter Jannah.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: مَنْ كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ
